intent: The deepest point in the ocean, Challenger Deep, is about 10,935 m down; Mount Everest is 8,849 m tall, so the whole mountain would sit under more than two kilometres of water.
pacing_profile: documentary: cold open, place, why in 2–5 beats, twist, close answers the open, short CTA (docs/STORY_GUIDELINES.md §2)
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses.
title: The hole that would swallow Everest

lines.direction: CRITICAL opener: high-altitude view of the western Pacific from the Philippines to the Marianas, then a hyper-smooth kinetic plunge straight down onto the empty blue of the trench as the neon trench line draws through; the pin pings on 'swallow'
lines.text: Somewhere under this patch of blue is a hole deep enough to swallow the tallest mountain on Earth.

lines.direction: pull back so the whole trench arc is in frame while the neon line redraws north; the TRENCH tag plates; a tracking pan north-east and the Guam pin pings
lines.text: This is Challenger Deep, at the southern end of the Mariana Trench, about 300 kilometres south-west of Guam.

lines.direction: short dive from Guam onto the Challenger Deep pin (k 3); the depth counter rolls to 10,935 in the clear water below the trench line as the camera keeps pushing; the pressure card follows once the counter is gone
lines.text: The sea floor here is about 10,935 metres down. Nearly eleven kilometres of water, pressing down with more than a thousand times the pressure at the surface.

lines.direction: one long, even pull-out from the trench until all of Asia is in frame with Everest at the far left; the Everest pin pings on '8,849' and the mountain rises beside the peak; on 'fly' it arcs across Asia along the dashed neon-blue line and the camera flies with it, centred on the mountain, descending onto the trench pin as it arrives
lines.text: Now take Mount Everest, 8,849 metres high, and fly it from the Himalaya to this spot.

lines.direction: the mountain falls into the trench spot with a splash and is gone; push in on the empty water; card with the 2 km margin
lines.text: Drop it in. The whole mountain disappears, and its summit would still be more than two kilometres under the surface.

lines.direction: answer the opening line with the same noun
lines.text: The deepest place on Earth: a hole so deep the highest mountain simply vanishes into it.

lines.direction: short follow — the outro visual does the work
lines.text: Follow for a new map story every day.
